question: Which storage granularity makes retained scalar analysis useful across representative admitted task shapes?
corpus: Pipelines at 8/16 helpers, imported fanout at 8/24 and mutual recursion at 8/12, with twice as many independent source files.
oracle: Independent Python execution and AST byte coordinates; every cached result must agree with clean analysis at the same revision.
measurements: worker and native child peak RSS
conditions: Separate fresh workers, isolated cache directories, identical native binary, disabled native fact cache, rotating strategy order, three repetitions. OS caches are not flushed. Tokens are unavailable.
edit_boundary: Direct edits for benchmark tooling, SDK cache encoding, regression tests and docs; the existing body writer does not express this integrated change.
claims: A finite structural corpus within the scalar subset; no production workload, population speedup, partial-summary reuse, live-agent or source-proof claim.
diagnostics: Initial storage probe used a rejected 16384-step request; corrected to 4096 before any measurements.
The 24-helper pipeline exceeded the response budget and is a boundary case. The measured pipeline uses 16 helpers.
The recursive corpus was expanded after the probe so each recursive pair participates in the entry query.
With all recursive pairs participating, 24 helpers also exceeded the response budget. The measured recursive cases use 8/12 helpers; 24 remains a boundary case.
